title: METHODOLOGY FIX: prior win-tests were oracle-contaminated; require HELD-OUT post-hoc grading
summary: Pivotal finding (8th no-win, wincase-c): the rigging guard caught that cold-B self-solves by REVERSE-ENGINEERING the strategy from the committed acceptance test. ROOT CAUSE: every bench v1–v8 shipped the acceptance test INTO the agent's worktree + told it "make this test pass" → the test IS the oracle → the agent derives the answer from it → context is never load-bearing. So NO prior run validly tested whether retrieving context HELPS THE AGENT SOLVE; that question is UNTESTED, not answered. WHAT SURVIVES (does not depend on the oracle): (a) cost findings (v2/v3 lean=cost-parity, cache_read is the cost story); (b) the over-deliberation finding + the GATE — actually reinforced, since the oracle made tasks self-solvable and context then added ~2x hardness = exactly the abstain regime the gate handles (regret=0). FIX (held-out protocol, per user directive "test only AFTER cold and warm finish"): agent solves from a PROSE SPEC ONLY — no test file, no 'make it pass', no scoring rubric in the worktree; it writes its best impl blind; THEN an external held-out test suite the agent never saw grades each artifact post-hoc. Same spec + same hidden grader for both arms; only difference = graph access. This makes the empirical note load-bearing (only way to know the held-out edge cases without seeing them). Harness change to bench-arm.js: strip the test from the solve worktree; add a post-solve external grade phase; 'solved' := passed held-out grader. Candidates: silent-cap (cap=50 unguessable AND held-out — strongest), task→transcript held-out (~40% correlation rows never shown), mutation-aliasing. Rigging guard now = cold reliably FAILS the held-out edge cases.
